subject.title: fix(slack): bound one-shot WebClient/write timeouts without Bolt deadline

question: Should OpenClaw adopt fixed 30-second web and 60-second write deadlines for independent Slack requests while preserving timeout-free shared Bolt options?
rationale: These new runtime defaults trade indefinite stalls for possible failures and ambiguous delivery on unusually slow Slack requests, so the values and intended affected clients require owner confirmation.

options.title: Isolate One-Shot Timeouts
options.body: Apply the 30-second deadline only in independent WebClient construction, keep Bolt options timeout-free, and retain the 60-second write deadline with current-head proof.

options.title: Include Bolt Requests
options.body: Intentionally give Bolt's WebClient the 30-second request deadline and add explicit upgrade rationale plus live proof for listener-driven API calls.

options.title: Defer Fixed Defaults
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until operational evidence establishes suitable deadlines and delivery-reconciliation behavior.

recommendation.title: Isolate One-Shot Timeouts
recommendation.body: Apply the 30-second deadline only in independent WebClient construction, keep Bolt options timeout-free, and retain the 60-second write deadline with current-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a compatibility-sensitive channel default decision that needs repository-level product ownership rather than contributor-only judgment.
